prov.text: Allowance for credit losses. The ACL is a reserve accumulated on the Consolidated Balance Sheets through the recognition of the provision for credit losses. First Financial records provision expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income to maintain the ACL at a level considered sufficient to absorb expected credit losses for financial assets over their expected remaining lives with consideration given to current and forward-looking information.

tax.heading: INCOME TAXES
tax.text:
Linked quarter comparison: In the third quarter of 2026, First Financial recorded income tax expense of $18.1 million on pre-tax income of $99.3 million, resulting in an effective tax rate of 18.2%. This compared to income tax expense of $18.0 million on pre-tax income of $94.4 million and an effective tax rate of 19.0% for the second quarter 2026. The lower effective tax rate in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by the recognition of certain solar tax credits during the third quarter.

Year-to-date comparison: For the first nine months of 2026, income tax expense was $55.2 million on pre-tax income of $287.3 million, resulting in an effective tax rate of 19.2%. This compared to income tax expense of $48.9 million on pre-tax income of $242.1 million and an effective tax rate of 20.2% for the comparable period in 2025. The lower effective tax rate in the first nine months of 2026 compared to 2025 was primarily driven by the nontaxable bargain purchase gain related to the BankFinancial acquisition and increased tax credit activity, which was partially offset by higher income and nondeductible charitable contributions.

The Company's effective tax rate may fluctuate from period to period due to changes in tax jurisdictions, forecasted income, tax-enhanced assets and tax credit investments.

net.text: All significant reclassifications of prior period amounts, if applicable, have been made to conform to the current period’s presentation and had no effect on the Company's previously reported net income or financial condition.

capex.text: Capital expenditures were $28.8 million and $12.7 million for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively. Management believes sufficient liquidity exists to fund its future capital expenditure commitments.

Net interest income.heading: NET INTEREST INCOME
Net interest income.text:
First Financial’s primary source of income is net interest income, which is the excess of interest received from earning assets, including loan-related fees and purchase accounting accretion, minus interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities. The amount of net interest income is determined by the volume and mix of earning assets, the rates earned on such assets and the volume, mix and rates paid for the deposits and borrowings that fund the earning assets. Earning assets primarily consist of interest-bearing loans and leases to customers, as well as marketable investment securities.

Noninterest income.heading: NONINTEREST INCOME
Noninterest income.text:
Linked quarter comparison: Third quarter 2026 noninterest income was $77.7 million, increasing $3.9 million, or 5.2%, compared to $73.8 million for the second quarter of 2026. The increase from the linked quarter was primarily driven by foreign exchange income, client derivative fees, wealth management fees, and bankcard income. These increases were partially offset by lower gain on bargain purchase and gains from loan sales.

Foreign exchange income increased $4.4 million, or 33.5%, and client derivative fees increased $1.1 million, or 74.0%, as client demand increased during the period. Wealth management fees increased $0.9 million, or 10.7%, from the second quarter due to higher investment banking and consulting fee income while bankcard income increased $0.8 million, or 27.4%, due to lower termination fees during the third quarter.

Partially offsetting these increases, gain on bargain purchase decreased $3.2 million, or 98.8%, due to fewer purchase accounting adjustments recognized on the BankFinancial transaction during the third quarter while gains from loan sales decreased $1.0 million, or 15.1%, due to a lower volume of sold loans.

intro.text: First Financial Bancorp., an Ohio corporation (First Financial or the Company), was formed in 1982. First Financial is a mid-sized, regional bank holding company headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, which has elected to become a financial holding company. References in this Form 10-K to “we,” “us” or “our” refer, as the context requires, to First Financial and its subsidiaries, collectively or to First Financial as the holding company. First Financial engages in the business of commercial banking and other banking and banking-related activities through its wholly-owned subsidiary, First Financial Bank (the Bank), which was founded in 1863. Effective December 30, 2016, the Bank converted its charter to an Ohio state chartered bank from a nationally chartered bank.
